case.title: Copy disguised by reordering, capitalisation and swapped stop words still fires

submissions.open_text: We queue at the kiosk in the morning and the jerrican costs shillings
In the Morning there is a Queue at our Kiosk and each Jerrican costs Shillings

case.why: A fabricator rewords a copied answer by reordering it, capitalising words and swapping filler words. After lowercasing and removing stop words (we/at/the/in/and/there/is/a/our/each), both texts give exactly {queue, kiosk, morning, jerrican, costs, shillings}, so the Jaccard similarity is 6/6 = 1.0 and the check fires. Wrong implementations stay silent: without stop-word removal the lowercased token sets give 10 shared of 16 = 0.625, and without lowercasing only 'costs' matches. Other checks are quiet: durations of 23 and 29 min, different days, daytime, points inside Nyalenda, E02 alone on the device, no transcript.
